title: GIAC GCED
summary: The GIAC Certified Enterprise Defender (GCED) is an advanced certification for defenders who must understand both how networks are attacked and how to stop those attacks. It suits experienced SOC analysts, incident responders, network security engineers and defenders preparing for a broad role rather than a single specialism. It proves to an employer that you can explain protocol weaknesses, choose detective and preventive controls, read packet captures, triage malware, and take part in a penetration test with a clear scope. The exam is a proctored, open book test of multiple choice questions taken from your own reference material, which rewards preparation with well indexed notes. GIAC does not publish domain weightings, so no percentages appear below, and the two malware analysis domains are presented together here. It leads to senior SOC analyst, incident response and defensive engineering roles. This is an independent study guide and it is not affiliated with GIAC or SANS.

beginner.definition: The GCED is a certification from GIAC about defending a whole company, not just one product. It covers how attackers move through a network. It also covers how defenders watch for them, stop them and learn from them. It is an advanced certification, so it expects you to already work in security. The exam is open book, which means you may bring your own notes.
beginner.whyItMatters: Defenders who understand the attacker's side make better decisions about what to fix first. This certification proves that breadth. That matters when you are the person who must explain risk to a manager. It is well respected because it comes from the organisation behind the well known SANS training courses. It supports movement into senior analyst and incident response roles. Open book means the exam rewards organised notes, so your preparation keeps its value.
howItWorks: Check that you meet the entry expectation first, because this is not a beginner certification.
Study the official objectives domain by domain. Note where your daily work already covers them.
Build a lab with a firewall, a packet capture tool and a malware analysis sandbox you control.
Index your notes carefully with tabs and a contents page, because you may use them during the exam.
Take the practice tests included with registration. Treat a low score as a study plan, not a verdict.
The exam itself is proctored and open book. It is mostly multiple choice, sat inside a fixed time window.
beginner.example: Imagine you are the only security engineer on duty. A supplier reports strange traffic coming to your network. You open a packet capture and see a regular connection to an unusual address every ten minutes. You check your intrusion detection system. It never alerted, because the rule was never tuned for that protocol. You block the address and add a rule so the same pattern is caught next time. GCED is about having the knowledge to do all three steps without waiting for help.
takeaways: This is an advanced exam, so build a base in security operations first.
Your notes are allowed in the exam, so index them properly while you study.
Understanding the attacker's method is what makes your defences targeted.

objectives: Explain how common network protocols work and how each one can be abused by an attacker.
Choose detective and preventive controls that fit a specific risk in a network or cloud environment.
Read a packet capture and describe what happened between two hosts.
Triage a suspicious file safely and describe what it does and what it leaves behind.
Follow a continuous incident response process from detection through to lessons learned.
Explain the scope, rules and reporting stages of a penetration test from the defender's point of view.
attributionNote: GIAC certification content is an independent study guide written for CyberPulseAcademy from the publicly published exam objectives. It is NOT official GIAC material. chapters.title: Defending Network Protocols
objectives: Explain how common protocols such as address resolution, name resolution and routing actually work.
Describe the attacks that target each of those protocols and the signs they leave in logs.
Apply audit techniques to check whether a network is configured as intended.
Use recognised hardening benchmarks and control frameworks to prioritise defensive work.

chapters.title: Defensive Infrastructure and Tactics
objectives: Describe preventive controls such as segmentation, filtering and access restriction and where each belongs.
Describe detective controls such as logging, monitoring and alerting and what each one can miss.
Explain how cloud infrastructure changes the way you apply those same controls.
Choose a control that reduces a stated risk and explain the trade off it introduces.

chapters.title: Digital Forensics Concepts and Application
objectives: Follow a sound process for identifying, collecting and preserving digital evidence.
Locate forensic artefacts on a system and explain what each one can prove.
Explain how the order of volatility decides what you collect first.
Describe how to keep evidence trustworthy from collection through to reporting.

chapters.title: Incident Response Concepts and Application
objectives: Explain the stages of a continuous incident response process and the goal of each stage.
Relate observed attacker activity to the stages of the Cyber Kill Chain.
Use threat intelligence to decide whether an alert deserves escalation.
Describe how lessons learned from one incident improve future detection.

chapters.title: Malware Analysis Concepts, Basic and Interactive Techniques
objectives: Identify the main types of malware and the symptoms each one causes on a host.
Analyse a suspicious file safely using an isolated environment made for that purpose.
Describe the benefits and limits of automated analysis tools and when to trust their output.
Observe a running sample in a controlled sandbox and record the behaviour you see.
Interpret the output of interactive tools such as process and registry monitors.
Recognise code obfuscation and describe the basic steps of manual code review.

chapters.title: Intrusion Detection and Packet Analysis
objectives: Explain where an intrusion detection or prevention system should sit in a network.
Tune a detection rule so that it catches the behaviour you care about without constant noise.
Investigate an alert and decide whether it is a true or false positive.
Take and read a packet capture to confirm what crossed the wire.

chapters.title: Network Security Monitoring Concepts and Application
objectives: Describe the devices a security operations centre uses to monitor a network.
Explain the packet and flow types that matter when you are hunting for intruders.
Explain the practice of continuous monitoring and what it requires from a team.
Describe the difficulties of monitoring traffic that is encrypted.

chapters.title: Network Forensics, Logging and Event Management
objectives: Use logs and flow records to reconstruct what happened during an incident.
Explain why central logging and time synchronisation are essential to an investigation.
Use a security information and event management system to search and correlate events.
Describe how security analytics differs from simple rule based alerting.

chapters.title: Penetration Testing Concepts
objectives: Explain the purpose of a scope agreement and rules of engagement before testing starts.
Describe the tools and tactics commonly used during a penetration test.
Explain how test results should be reported to technical and non technical readers.
Describe the legal and ethical limits that apply to any testing activity.

chapters.title: Penetration Testing Application
objectives: Demonstrate common testing tactics against a typical target system in a lab.
Use standard testing tools to find and confirm a weakness.
Explain how a tester records evidence of a finding without causing damage.
Describe how defensive teams can use a test report to close the gaps it names.
